- If sentiment is consistently negative or low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and prices are trending upward, model often over-optimistically forecasts continuation; cap upward slope at 1–2% per day.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; add a 1–3 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting toward historical mean), check if sentiment supports it — if not, reduce mean-reversion strength by 20–40%.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows volatility >15% from 10-day average, model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast spread by 10–20%.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to err on the side of overconfidence; apply a 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
